component: Core event engine, journal and timeframe store
evidence: No-op 10k run retained 10,002 events and one equity point per bar; cProfile at 5k attributed material time to timeframe push, equity recording, event emission and deep-freeze. Journal keeps projections plus event sequence/ID/entity indexes; JsonLinesEventStore also retains an internal InMemoryEventStore.
proposed_action: Introduce bounded/streaming observability contracts, bounded HTF/base histories and compact equity storage while preserving canonical audit mode; verify exact trade/event equivalence.
expected_effect: Remove multiplicative per-bar retention and make memory proportional to configured bounds rather than total history.
risk: High: observability and replay semantics can drift.
acceptance_criteria: 10k/50k/100k/250k scale ladder within explicit RSS limits; exact fills/trades/final equity and canonical evidence equivalence; restart determinism.

evidence: Full registered BTC incident reached ~65.2 GB physical footprint and ~64.5 GB swap. Local base benchmark: 10k no-op 4.436 s, ~139.8 MiB RSS, 10,002 events; 5k checkpoint mode 6.631 s and ~20.48 MiB traced peak versus 2.146 s/~5.85 MiB single pass.
proposed_action: Complete and independently validate Draft PR #287: research_fast bounded mode, append-only bounded journal, sampled equity, aggregated skips, one-pass checkpoint-disabled execution, memory guards and later true streaming input.
expected_effect: Prevent host exhaustion and GC thrashing; enable multi-year registered-dataset research on bounded hardware.
risk: High: execution, checkpoint and audit artifact equivalence.
acceptance_criteria: No OOM/swap storm; scale thresholds; full BTC completes under configured memory guard; exact trade equivalence; canonical mode remains available.

component: Registered dataset → Backtest bridge and loader
evidence: Static path materializes validated candles into a list and HistoricalDataFeed converts the iterable to a tuple before Core validation/replay; external registration helpers also use whole-file read_bytes and Arrow to_pylist per source file.
proposed_action: Add iterator/record-batch ingestion with streaming manifest accumulation and column pruning; retain immutable dataset identity and exact validation.
expected_effect: Eliminate final full Candle-list copies and lower peak memory/I/O amplification for multi-symbol histories.
risk: High: ordering, gap and hash semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Byte/row/hash identity unchanged; gap/duplicate rejection unchanged; peak RSS bounded across scale ladder; identical Backtest outputs.

evidence: Real BTCUSDT 5m evidence: 721,597 rows, 83 partitions, 1,101.233 s (~655 rows/s), sampled RSS ~297 MiB. Validation 444.89 s, source decode/spool 226.50 s, publish 210.96 s, checksum reread 218.56 s. Memory is bounded, throughput is I/O/validation constrained.
proposed_action: Profile validation/checksum phases, avoid redundant rereads where integrity permits, batch vectorizable checks, and split 1,017-line execute method behind unchanged contracts.
expected_effect: Reduce ingestion wall time without increasing memory or weakening checks.
risk: Medium: data integrity and atomic publication.
acceptance_criteria: Same manifests/checksums/repair decisions; >=25% wall-time improvement on fixed corpus; RSS does not regress >10%.

evidence: Persistent smoke passed for 10 datasets, 12,968,018 rows and 3,865 partitions. Static audit found full-file read_bytes/hash comparisons in some external registration paths, but no demonstrated registry bottleneck.
proposed_action: Add registry query/registration latency and peak-RSS benchmarks before changing storage; replace full-file reads only where measurement confirms value.
expected_effect: Evidence for future corpus growth; possible lower peak memory during registration.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark published; same dataset_id/version/hash conflict rules; atomic crash tests remain green.

component: Market Data CLI, API, jobs and Web Console
evidence: Control-plane, browser E2E, durable update/backfill/repair and security workflows are green. Large DatasetOperations/IngestionService/BinanceAdapter/LocalStorage classes increase change risk, but no measured user-facing latency bottleneck was found.
proposed_action: Add API/CLI latency and job-queue saturation telemetry; decompose by responsibility only with contract tests.
expected_effect: Improved maintainability/observability rather than speculative speedup.
acceptance_criteria: No API/CLI contract drift; latency dashboards and regression thresholds; all durable job/restart tests pass.

evidence: Extensive deterministic scheduler, lease fencing, restart and package tests are green. Thread/process execution exists, but no exact integrated multi-process serialization/RSS benchmark was found in the audited base.
proposed_action: Benchmark process-pool payload serialization, queue depth, worker RSS and multi-experiment throughput before concurrency changes.
expected_effect: Prevent premature parallelism changes and identify true orchestration limits.
acceptance_criteria: Scale curves for 1/2/4 workers; stale worker rejection unchanged; deterministic artifacts identical.

evidence: Fast CI and immutable package validation are green; existing issues document prior producer/consumer version skew, now integrated. No current throughput/RSS bottleneck was measured.
proposed_action: Add package intake, SQLite registration and query benchmarks at increasing experiment counts; retain fail-closed schema compatibility sets.
expected_effect: Evidence-based capacity planning and early detection of registry growth issues.
acceptance_criteria: Latency percentiles and DB-size curves recorded; DUPLICATE/conflict semantics unchanged.

evidence: Measured evidence includes 10k canonical hashes in 6.64 s, 500 artifact cycles in 1.45 s, 2k idempotency cycles in 0.33 s and traced peak near 215 KiB; CI/hardening/soak are green.
proposed_action: Retain current design and monitor only; do not rewrite.
expected_effect: Avoid low-value churn.
acceptance_criteria: Existing benchmark thresholds and exact evidence hashes remain stable.

evidence: Package gates are green; one package job took 200 s and another 125 s on the exact base, but duration includes environment/build work and does not prove runtime algorithm bottleneck.
proposed_action: Separate installation/build time from audit-decision runtime and add evidence-package size ladder.
expected_effect: Clarify whether optimization belongs in CI packaging or audit validation.
risk: High if authorization semantics are changed.
acceptance_criteria: Decision content/signature/reason codes identical; benchmark isolates CPU/I/O/install phases.

evidence: Python 3.12/3.13 CI, replay, reconciliation and fail-closed tests are green. No production-like order-volume latency/RSS SLO was found.
proposed_action: Add order/fill/reconciliation throughput and SQLite growth benchmarks before optimization.
expected_effect: Capacity evidence without risking lifecycle correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Exact order/fill projections and recovery equivalence at increasing event volumes.

evidence: Lifecycle/recovery/supervision gates pass; paper-only boundary is explicit. No long multi-symbol staging latency and memory profile was available.
proposed_action: Instrument event-loop lag, queue depth, checkpoint duration and per-symbol state during staging soak.
expected_effect: Detect operational saturation before changing architecture.
acceptance_criteria: Published SLOs; restart and shutdown ordering unchanged; paper-only enforcement remains structural.

evidence: Local smoke suite passed in ~5.25 s with peak RSS ~199 MiB; exact base CI is green. No high fan-out/chat benchmark was found.
proposed_action: Measure rendering/send queue latency only if usage grows; retain configuration-controlled optional status.
expected_effect: Avoid unnecessary optimization.
acceptance_criteria: No message deduplication or authorization regression.

evidence: 349-test final evidence, fuzz/stress/replay are documented; large route methods (up to ~484 LOC/62 branch nodes) are maintainability hotspots. No production latency/RSS SLO was found.
proposed_action: Add route latency distribution and refactor high-complexity branches only behind golden replay tests.
expected_effect: Lower change risk; performance only if benchmark shows regression.
acceptance_criteria: Bit-for-bit equivalent plans and reason codes across golden corpus; no latency regression.

evidence: 50k plans ~8.04 s (~6,220/s); 250k ~40.81 s; bounded state with ~17.1 MiB traced peak and ~67.1 MiB RSS in stress evidence.
proposed_action: Keep current implementation; monitor benchmark.
expected_effect: Avoid speculative rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: Existing performance and deterministic contract gates remain stable.

evidence: Million-event/bounded-state evidence and Python 3.12/3.13 gates are present; exact-base CI succeeded.
proposed_action: Monitor only.
expected_effect: No unnecessary semantic risk.
acceptance_criteria: Keep million-event and deterministic restart gates.

evidence: Pure numeric logic, extensive precision/boundary/adversarial tests and no measured bottleneck; only one small duplicated helper group was detected.
proposed_action: Do not optimize; optionally consolidate duplicate helper during unrelated maintenance.
expected_effect: Preserve numerical semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Exact Decimal/rounding outputs unchanged.

evidence: Existing heavy evidence reports bounded state and high throughput; exact base integration gates are green.
proposed_action: Monitor only.
expected_effect: Avoid churn.

evidence: Evidence ranges from ~13.8k no-op events/s to ~50k+/s at larger active workloads with bounded state; CI and recovery gates are green.

evidence: Small adapter surface (~917 source LOC), deterministic contracts and green integrated acceptance; no bottleneck evidence.

evidence: ~11,061 calls/s in 20k×2 evidence, traced peak ~62.9 KiB and checkpoint 3,438 bytes.

evidence: ~11k calls/s through 250k workload with ~7.7 KiB rolling traced state and deterministic restart. restore_state is a complexity hotspot (~401 LOC/132 branches), but performance is adequate.
proposed_action: No performance rewrite; later split state restoration with golden snapshots.

evidence: Quality/hardening gates are green; no measured runtime bottleneck. Module class is large (~1,390 LOC/51 methods), making maintainability—not speed—the concern.
proposed_action: Refactor only along existing state-machine boundaries with replay goldens.
expected_effect: Lower maintenance risk.
acceptance_criteria: Exact decision/reason/checkpoint equivalence.

evidence: 100k bars ~24.76 s (~4,039/s); 1m chunked median ~4,025/s; bounded state ~316 KiB. Longest workflow wall time was 901 s, but slowest actual job 337 s includes full quality/package gates.
proposed_action: Keep runtime; optimize CI setup only if needed.
expected_effect: Avoid algorithm churn.
acceptance_criteria: Retain 1m bounded-state evidence.

evidence: Runtime gates and deep hardening are green; CI quality jobs took 197/190 s and workflow wall 830 s, pointing primarily to CI setup duplication rather than algorithm evidence.
proposed_action: Keep module runtime; reduce repeated CI installation/package steps centrally.
expected_effect: Faster feedback without trading semantic changes.
acceptance_criteria: Same quality gates with lower summed job time.

evidence: Dedicated module CI succeeded on exact base; no bottleneck evidence was found.
proposed_action: Monitor only.
expected_effect: Avoid speculative optimization.
acceptance_criteria: Existing module and integration gates remain green.

evidence: Base has 59 workflows; exact SHA produced 50 runs/84 jobs, 5,213 job-seconds (~1.45 h), 12.16 MB artifacts; only ~22 s ran hosted. 40 jobs do not invoke the mandated reusable Python preflight, many repeat installs, and many external Actions use mutable tags. One Core run failed because a runner reported 0 GiB free; a parallel run succeeded.
proposed_action: Create reusable component quality workflows/actions, pin external Actions to immutable SHAs, normalize preflight, narrow triggers, cancel obsolete duplicates and record setup/test phase timings.
expected_effect: Lower self-hosted queue pressure and flaky infrastructure failures; faster feedback; stronger supply-chain reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: No gate removal; >=30% lower summed job-time on unchanged source; no duplicate same-SHA runs; all Actions pinned; all Python jobs use approved preflight.

evidence: 549 test files and strong component coverage. Naive repo-wide pytest collection fails on duplicate module basenames and optional dependencies; CI works by isolated subprocess suites.
proposed_action: Adopt importlib test import mode or unique package namespaces, formalize smoke/unit/integration/nightly markers and keep isolated dependency extras explicit.
expected_effect: Simpler local reproduction and fewer collection surprises without deleting tests.
acceptance_criteria: One documented root collection command succeeds; existing isolated suite counts unchanged; no tests silently omitted.

evidence: 21 separately packaged projects, broad minimum dependency ranges and no repository lockfile were found. Offline editable install could not satisfy isolated setuptools build requirements in the audit container; authoritative online CI is green.
proposed_action: Define a reproducible CI constraints/lock strategy per supported Python version while keeping library metadata ranges; cache wheels/build envs.
expected_effect: Faster, more reproducible installs and fewer dependency-drift failures.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh 3.12/3.13 installs reproduce; pip-audit/SBOM remain green; package consumers are not over-pinned.

component: Security, secret handling and supply chain
evidence: Static AST scan found no eval/exec/os.system, unsafe pickle/yaml, shell=True or obvious literal secrets in production; release readiness secret-pattern checks passed. Mutable Action tags remain the main identified supply-chain gap.
proposed_action: Pin Actions by SHA, retain dependency/SBOM/secret gates and periodically verify permissions/retention.
expected_effect: Stronger reproducibility and reduced upstream action compromise risk.
acceptance_criteria: All third-party Actions immutable; least-privilege permissions; security gates unchanged.

evidence: Full-RC ledger, release-readiness evidence and paper-only governance are strong. Numerous historical branches/issues increase navigation cost, but no runtime bottleneck.
proposed_action: Archive/label stale workstreams after governance approval and keep a single current component/performance ledger.
expected_effect: Lower coordination overhead.
acceptance_criteria: No history deletion; canonical current-state links remain valid.
